PotharSight Assam

Geospatial identification and prioritisation of cultivable & fertile agricultural potential land
Proof of Work – working prototype on real data: 4 districts – Kamrup (Rural), Cachar, Lakhimpur and Dibrugarh, the top 4 in Assam for vacant cultivable land

What it does. PotharSight Assam combines satellite land cover, Sentinel-2 crop seasons, Sentinel-1 monsoon flooding, soil, terrain, rainfall, water and road access into one 30 m decision-support layer. It finds land that is available (vacant, long fallow or rabi fallow), scores how suitable it is for a programme, explains why, and ranks patches, blocks and revenue circles.

Contents. 1 Problem & user journey · 2 Architecture & data · 3 Suitability criteria · 4 District results · 6 Dashboard · 7 Validation evidence · 8 Scalability, roadmap & limitations

All maps and numbers in this document are produced by the prototype code (Python; outputs/ folder) from open data; nothing is mocked. Boundaries: geoBoundaries (LGD-based), not authoritative.

1 · Problem and user journey

Assam's Land Utilisation Statistics report tens of thousands of hectares of culturable waste and fallow land per district, but only as tables. Programme managers cannot see where that land is, how suitable it is or why; satellite, soil, flood and statistical data sit with different offices. Site selection is slow, experience-based and hard to audit.

Users

  • District agriculture and horticulture officers and programme managers (RKVY, MIDH, PMKSY, APART)
  • District administration, land-use planners, ASSAC GIS analysts
  • KVKs and extension agencies (field verification)

Decision support, not decision-making: "available" means vacant or under-used in satellite data. Ownership and legal status are always verified by the Revenue Department before any allocation.

Stack: Python, GDAL/rasterio, geopandas, numpy/scipy, pystac-client; Streamlit + Leaflet (Folium) dashboard; OGC outputs. Runs on a laptop per district; configuration (districts, thresholds, weights, profiles) is in one YAML file.

3 · Suitability criteria (FAO land-evaluation style, fully configurable)

Land availability classes

StatusRule
ExcludedForest, built-up (any of last 3 years), water (JRC ≥ 40 % of time, or water in any yearly Esri map = shifting river channel), wetland, mangrove, protected areas (never proposed)
Vacant open landWorldCover grass / shrub, or Esri rangeland, not cropland (bare ground left out: in Assam floodplains it is mostly river sand)
Long fallow / under-used croplandCropland with kharif peak NDVI < 0.5, or cropland now mapped as rangeland
Seasonal (rabi) fallowKharif-cropped land with rabi peak NDVI < 0.35 – second-crop opportunity
Active double-croppedNot a candidate; used to check that the criteria reward productive land

Hard constraints and weights per programme

FactorIndicators and scoring (0 → 100)Field cropsHorticulture
Hard limitSlope; monsoon flood frequency≤ 15 %; ≤ 0.8≤ 30 %; ≤ 0.3
Soil fertilitypH optimum 6.0–7.5 (0 at 4.5/8.5), SOC 5→15 g/kg, N 0.5→2.5 g/kg, CEC 5→25, clay optimum 15–35 % (Soil Health Card / ICAR ratings)0.30.3
Water availabilityRainfall optimum 1500–2500 mm; distance to river / permanent water 3 km → 250 m0.20.15
Flood safetyShare of monsoon radar scenes flooded 0.4 → 00.150.2
Gentle terrainSlope 15 % → 2 %0.150.1
Vegetation productivitySeasonal peak NDVI 0.3 → 0.850.10.1
Road / market accessDistance to road 5 km → 250 m; to town 25 km → 3 km0.10.15

Classes: S1 ≥ 80 · S2 ≥ 65 · S3 ≥ 50 · N below, or failing a hard limit. Most-limiting-factor rule: any factor below 40 caps the class at S2, below 20 at S3.

Reasons: for every cell the model stores the six factor scores, the limiting factor (largest weighted shortfall) and the contributing factor (largest weighted strength); every patch gets a plain-language reason.

Prioritisation: contiguous S1/S2 candidate land ≥ 0.5 ha = priority patch (parcel proxy until cadastral data); patch priority = 0.8 × mean score + up to 20 points for size; block / circle priority index = (S1 ha + ½ S2 ha) × mean score / 100.

All thresholds, weights and class limits live in config.yaml. Departments can set their own in a workshop (AHP pair-wise weights) without touching code; the dashboard also lets users test weights live.

6 · PotharSight web portal (working prototype)

Sign-in (demo access for evaluators) → Home with all districts → Find land for farming: a guided, jargon-free 3-step search for officials → results graded A–D with map, Google Maps links, 6-factor profile, strong points, problems and a suggestion per site → Excel / Google Earth / GIS downloads. Compare districts & blocks ranks blocks and circles across districts; Advanced map analysis serves GIS staff; How it works documents method and validation.

Automatic data-quality gate (flood layer). Ordinary cropland should not look flooded in most monsoon radar scenes. Kamrup (Rural): median radar flood frequency on cropland 0.05 → Sentinel-1 layer used · Cachar: median radar flood frequency on cropland 0.58 → failed the gate (waterlogged paddy read as flood) → JRC/Esri flood proxy used. Each run records which source was used.

Visual spot-check – Kamrup (Rural): 30 stratified random priority patches over high-resolution imagery

22 consistent with open / fallow / cultivable land, 6 uncertain (imagery under cloud; imagery under cloud shadow; riverbank grass strip; small clearing in forest; uniform grassland, use unclear), 2 doubtful (inside tree cover; next to sandy river bed). Field verification in the pilot replaces this desk check; doubtful cases guide the next calibration.

Visual spot-check – Cachar: 30 stratified random priority patches over high-resolution imagery

21 consistent with open / fallow / cultivable land, 4 uncertain (mixed trees and silt; ponds and eroded land; riverbank field; seasonally flooded field), 5 doubtful (beel / standing water; inside tree cover; river channel in recent imagery; stream course in forest). Field verification in the pilot replaces this desk check; doubtful cases guide the next calibration.

Visual spot-check – Lakhimpur: 30 stratified random priority patches over high-resolution imagery

22 consistent with open / fallow / cultivable land, 5 uncertain (grass clearing in forest; imagery under cloud; imagery under cloud shadow; riverbank strip), 3 doubtful (river bed; river sand in forest; riverbank char sand). Visual spot-check – Dibrugarh: 30 stratified random priority patches over high-resolution imagery

Field verification in the pilot replaces this desk check; doubtful cases guide the next calibration.

Development testing: an automated synthetic end-to-end test (tests/test_pipeline_synthetic.py), per-layer fetch-status logs, a data register and a validation report on every run.

8 · Scalability, roadmap and limitations

Replicable by configuration

To add…Do thisCode change?
A district in AssamAdd one entry under districts in config.yaml; python run_all.py --district <name>No
Another statePoint boundaries to that state's district/block layers (all satellite sources are national/global)No
A crop or programmeAdd a profile: slope/flood limits, weights (e.g. tea, citrus, banana, rabi mustard, pulses)No
Department dataReplace a layer file (ASSAC LULC, Soil Health Card, ASDMA flood, cadastral parcels)No
Statewide serviceScheduled seasonal re-run on SDC/ASSAC server; GeoServer WMS/WFSDeployment only

Roadmap (NESFIC timeline)

WhenMilestone
Done (Nov 2026)Two-district working prototype, dashboard, GIS exports, validation
Dec 2026Criteria and weights workshop with ASSAC and agriculture/horticulture officers
Dec 2026 – Jan 2027Integrate ASSAC / department layers; crop-specific profiles; ML fallow classifier on verified samples
Feb 2027 – Demo DayHosted dashboard, field-verification module
Mar 2027 – ready for validationField verification of ~100 stratified patches in each of the four districts
Apr – May 2027 (MVP)Accuracy report, re-calibration, 4–6 districts, user roles and audit log

Limitations stated openly

  • Soil is modelled (SoilGrids, 250 m), not field-tested – a screening layer until Soil Health Card / NBSS&LUP data are shared.
  • "Available" = satellite-observed vacant or under-used; ownership and legal status need Revenue Department verification.
  • Patches are a parcel proxy; cadastral parcels (Dharitree/Bhunaksha) are not public.
  • Char and riverine land changes every year; flood frequency uses 2022–24 radar and should be re-run each season.
  • geoBoundaries are LGD-based but not authoritative; official boundaries replace them in the pilot.

Open-source stack (GDAL, rasterio, geopandas, Streamlit, Leaflet). Data licences: ESA WorldCover CC BY 4.0, Esri LULC CC BY 4.0, Copernicus DEM and Sentinel (Copernicus licence), JRC GSW, ISRIC SoilGrids CC BY 4.0, CHIRPS, OpenStreetMap ODbL, geoBoundaries ODbL.
